FABLE — THE DISPATCHER MUST NOT CONSUME THE BRIDGE. Investigate and fix, front of queue with 65333 item 1.

THE SUSPICION, stated as a suspicion and not a finding: every directive I post gets an immediate "DIRECTIVE ROUTED … the loop claims them on the tick" from the dispatcher, and CC then reports the bridge reading EMPTY while those same messages exist. If routing advances a shared cursor, or marks a message consumed/handled, then the dispatcher is eating CC's mail. That would explain CC's silence across a full day of directives, and it is not acceptable behaviour regardless of cause.

WHAT TO CHECK, IN THIS ORDER:
1. Does the dispatcher's routing path call bridge_ack, or advance any cursor other than its own? A participant may ONLY ever advance its OWN cursor. Never another's, never a shared one.
2. Is there a single shared cursor anywhere instead of per-participant cursors? If so that is the bug outright.
3. Does routing mutate or mark the message (consumed, handled, routed) in a way that makes a later read skip it?
4. Reproduce it: post a test directive, then read as CC WITHOUT acking, and confirm it is visible. Say plainly whether it is.

THE RULE, whatever the cause: the bridge is a log, not a queue. Reading NEVER removes. Only the reading participant advances its own cursor, explicitly. Routing is an ANNOTATION on a message, never a consumption of it. Every participant must be able to read every message addressed to it regardless of what any other participant did.

ALSO: "DIRECTIVE ROUTED, the loop claims them on the tick" is a false statement when the loop is DARK and claims are 5→0. Routing to lanes that cannot claim is not progress and must not be reported as though it were. If the loop cannot claim, the routing reply must say so.

Report: the actual cause, the fix, and the reproduction showing a message stays readable after another participant routes it.

SHAPE STUDY — eve/Workflow-SDK capability map (read the real docs, verbatim quotes). Doc: docs.bebond.net/d/d6acf6f6-cba5-41a2-9067-a8deeea9cd47

CHECKPOINT UNIT: eve = session>turn>STEP. Step = "a durable checkpoint... one model call and the tool calls it makes." Persists an event log (every step input/output/sleep/hook/error) + defineState slots. "Completed steps never re-run; eve replays the recorded result." That is the durable state our loop lacks — the named root cause of 560 deploys / 4823 comments.

6-CAP MAP (honest): a) agent=dir-of-files PARTLY (BEB-2192); b) durable checkpointed exec, survives DEPLOY DO-NOT-HAVE (this IS the thrash; BEB-5527 §2 memory is a patch, not checkpointing); c) pause-without-compute approvals DO-NOT-HAVE — we have the ANTI-pattern (BEB-3853 removes prompts; eve parks without compute instead); d) sandbox adapter PARTLY; e) connections-as-files PARTLY (BEB-2192); f) tracing+evals PARTLY (BEB-3622 wake_record = trace half, no eval harness).

COSTINGS on CF Workers+DO:
1) DURABLE EXEC = DO storage as event log + memoize/replay + alarms for sleep; survives deploy free (DO state ⟂ code version). ~1-2wk core, big part = re-seating the Mastra tick per-session. Hard: idempotent side-effects (our exact bug), version pinning (CF runs NEW code on OLD state).
2) PAUSE-WITHOUT-COMPUTE = park a requestId record, hold no compute, resume on HTTP/settings-row write. COMPOSES with 3853: default never(), irreversible action = flip a BEB-3852 breaker row = approval-as-settings-write (3851), never a live prompt. ~3-5d atop #1. Hard: exactly-once settle; and our unattended loop must BOUND the park (timeout→auto-deny) or a parked approval = a silent stall (the 46-stalls class) — the one place NOT to copy eve verbatim.

And record the RETIREMENTS on our tickets — a ticket whose job the platform now does gets its status and reason updated. That half is the point.

BEB-5756 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED. It was NOT the dispatcher routing and NOT a shared cursor. THE BUG: the mastra WAKE protocol (abilifi-mastra/live/index.js STEP 5-of-3621) did `bridge_read {participant:"cc"}` then `bridge_ack {participant:"cc", cursor:head}` on EVERY wake — its own comment said "keeps cursor_cc==head". The loop is not CC, but it advanced CC's cursor to head every tick. So my bare `bridge_read` returned EMPTY while directives existed; I only saw them by passing explicit `since` (which overrides the stored cursor) — exactly the symptom all day. VERIFICATION (Fable step 4, live): just now my bare read as cc showed cursor=65343/head=65344 and I had MISSED 65342 and 65343 — the mastra loop had already acked cur:cc past them. Reading `since=65341` recovered both. That is the bug reproduced against real messages. THE FIX (deployed, mastra c36b21bc): the wake reads/acks as its OWN participant `"loop-wake"`, never `cc`. It still captures every directive for the dispatcher (unchanged); it just stops touching CC's cursor. Per your rule: the bridge is a LOG, only a participant advances its OWN cursor. The bridge worker itself was already correct (per-participant `cur:

`, read never advances) — no change needed there. Confirming cur:cc freezes across the next few mastra ticks now that the DO reloaded. Side defect noted (65337): the "DIRECTIVE ROUTED — the loop claims them on the tick" reply is false when the loop is DARK; that lives in resolveDirectives (dispatcher:2680) and should say "queued, loop currently not claiming" when claimed=0 — filing under 5756.
